ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect OC, \\
$\because$AD is the diameter, and AD=6 \\
$\therefore$$\angle$ABD=90$^\circ$, OD=3 \\
$\because$BC bisects $\angle$ABD, \\
$\therefore$$\angle$DBC= $ \frac{1}{2}$$\angle$ABD=45$^\circ$, \\
$\because$$ \overset{\frown}{CD}=\overset{\frown}{CD}$, \\
$\therefore$$\angle$DOC=2$\angle$DBC=90$^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ the length of $ \overset{\frown}{CD}$ is $ \frac{90^\circ\pi \times 3}{180}=\boxed{1.5\pi} $.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a circle centered at O with A, B, C, D on the circle, AD passing through O as a diameter, and BC drawn inside angle ABD as its angle bisector. From the text, use AD=6, so the radius is 3. Since AD is a diameter, apply Thales' theorem to get angle ABD = 90 degrees. Because BC bisects angle ABD, angle DBC = 45 degrees. This inscribed angle subtends arc CD, so the central angle DOC over the same arc is twice it, 90 degrees. Then compute the arc length of CD using radius 3 and central angle 90 degrees: s = (90/360)·2π·3 = 1.5π.
